{"kind":"proof","text":"For each \(x\in[0,1)\), \(x^n\to 0\), while \(f_n(1)=1\) for every \(n\). Hence the pointwise limit is
\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}0,&0\le x<1,\\1,&x=1.\end{cases}
\]
If \((f_n)\) converged uniformly, its uniform limit would necessarily be \(f\). Set \(\varepsilon=\tfrac12\). For every \(N\in\mathbb Z_+\), choose \(n=N\) and \(x=2^{-1/N}\in[0,1)\). Then \(f(x)=0\) and
\[
|f_n(x)-f(x)|=x^N=\frac12.
\]
Thus, for every \(N\), there exist \(n\ge N\) and \(x\in[0,1]\) such that \(|f_n(x)-f(x)|\ge\varepsilon\), contradicting the definition of uniform convergence. Therefore \((f_n)\) does not converge uniformly on \([0,1]\).","reason":"The pointwise limit is identified, and the negation of uniform convergence is verified with a fixed positive epsilon."}

{"problem": {"theorem": "Define $f_{n}:[0,1] \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ by the equation $f_{n}(x)=x^{n}$. Show that the sequence $\left(f_{n}\right)$ does not converge uniformly.", "assumptions": [], "domain": "topology", "proof_text": "\begin{proof}

    The sequence $\left(f_n\right)_n$ does not converge uniformly, since given $0<\varepsilon<1$ and $N \in \mathbb{Z}_{+}$, for $x=\varepsilon^{1 / N}$ we have $d\left(f_N(x), f(x)\right)=\varepsilon$. We can also apply Theorem 21.6: the convergence is not uniform since $f$ is not continuous.

\end{proof}", "explicit_subgoals": []}, "rule_candidates": [{"id": "grp_first_iso", "name": "First isomorphism theorem for groups", "statement": "If phi: G -> H is a group homomorphism, then G/ker(phi) is isomorphic to im(phi).", "conditions": ["phi is a group homomorphism", "ker(phi) is the kernel of phi"], "conclusion": "G/ker(phi) is isomorphic to im(phi).", "rule_digest": "335c687d26f64e41584f1b8bc575aec9d78223b01c4821bf0056bf8533de0c19", "applicability": "unchecked"}, {"id": "grp_normal_quotient", "name": "Quotient group criterion", "statement": "If N is a normal subgroup of G, then the set of left cosets G/N forms a group under (aN)(bN) = abN.", "conditions": ["N is a subgroup of G", "N is normal in G"], "conclusion": "G/N is a group and coset multiplication is well-defined.", "rule_digest": "f6d458aa2e7463efeea7a535cdbe0f0f7930259cfe7f845b5350ec03454da876", "applicability": "unchecked"}, {"id": "grp_lagrange", "name": "Lagrange theorem", "statement": "If G is a finite group and H is a subgroup of G, then |H| divides |G|.", "conditions": ["G is finite", "H is a subgroup of G"], "conclusion": "|H| divides |G|.", "rule_digest": "361a6b53eb7c1cb71cc90836aab9022d76163052528c559907341ebabe9bf547", "applicability": "unchecked"}], "draft": "For each x∈[0,1), we have x^n→0, while f_n(1)=1 for every n.
